title: Policy-driven canary scheduler and safety guardrails
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a declarative canary configuration and runtime policy engine that encodes traffic-split schedules, step windows, metric guardrails, and automatic rollback behavior for model rollouts. The engine will be surfaced through both the Redwood Console (rollout UI) and the public API so customers can define canary strategies for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Goals: 1) support arbitrary step schedules (weights, durations, warmup), 2) express safety checks (latency P95, token error rate, hallucination proxy), 3) allow shadow/A-B/experiment modes, 4) make auto-rollback decisions auditable and configurable. This ticket scopes the core policy schema, runtime enforcement hooks, and a minimal console flow for creating a canary policy. Implementation will use existing rollout orchestration primitives but introduce a policy evaluation service that runs per-release and emits decisions and signals to the traffic router.
acceptance_criteria: Schema: A documented JSON/YAML canary_policy schema exists with fields for steps (weight, duration_ms/seconds), step_type (linear|exponential|custom), metric_checks (metric_name, comparator, threshold, window_sec, min_samples), and actions (promote, hold, rollback, alert).

Runtime: The policy engine evaluates a canary for a test model and exercises a 4-step linear schedule via automated integration tests simulating metrics; expected transitions occur when checks pass and rollback triggers when checks fail.
API: POST /rollouts/{id}/policy accepts the policy, returns 200, and stores policy as part of rollout metadata; GET returns current step and reason.
Console: Basic canary creation flow exposes weight sliders and a 'Safety checks' section with at least latency and error-rate presets.
Observability: Each policy evaluation emits events (policy.eval.start, policy.eval.result, policy.action) to the existing tracing pipeline and appears on the rollout trace.
tasks: Draft canary_policy schema and share with PM/design for feedback
Implement policy evaluator service that accepts policy + metrics snapshot and returns decision
Wire evaluator outputs into traffic router to change traffic split atomically
Add unit/integration tests that simulate metric regressions and assert rollback
Console: minimal form and preview of schedule; hook to create policy via API
Add tracing/logging and dashboard tile for policy actions and recent rollouts
Security review and threat model for policy APIs and rollout control plane
comments: 2025-02-25 Asha Patel: Created ticket after PM sync. Initial draft of schema attached in links. Goal is to reduce on-call regressions caused by bad model updates.

2025-02-27 Miguel Santos: Spike completed — evaluator implemented as a stateless service that consumes metric windows and returns one of {promote, hold, rollback, wait}. Worked through edge cases for insufficient samples.

2025-03-01 PM review (Lina Huang): Suggest adding a confidence threshold (statistical significance) for noisy metrics and a minimum-sample requirement to avoid flapping. Also requested shadow traffic mode for offline evaluation.
2025-03-03 Design feedback (Ravi Kapoor): UI needs a compact way to express multi-metric guardrails; proposed presets (slo-safe, permissive, strict). Logged wireframes in links.

2025-03-05 Miguel Santos: Implemented exponential schedule option and cooldown window. Started wiring policy events to tracing. Blocking on a small change to the traffic router API (atomic-split endpoint).
notes: Policy evaluation must be idempotent — evaluations may re-run from stored metric snapshots during replay.

Auto-rollback will produce an audit entry and trigger escalation (pager) only if the policy 'rollback' action is set to 'enforce'; otherwise it should only create an annotation and alert on the dashboard.
Consider supporting simulated rollouts (dry-run) where decisions are logged but not applied — useful for policy tuning on historical data.
We should expose a rate-limiter on API to prevent abusive rapid changes to live traffic splits in high-frequency environments.
